newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt borrowing need seen falling - agency.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt borrowing need seen falling - agency.

text.p: The Swedish government will in its spring budget proposal, due to be released at 1100 GMT, forecast its borrowing requirement will fall from 1997 to the year 2000, Swedish news agency TT reported on Tuesday.
This year, the government expects to borrow 26 billion crowns and in 1998 and 1999 it sees a borrowing need of nine billion crowns annually, the agency said.
In the year 2000, there will be no need to borrow. Instead the government could, if it wants to, use six billion crowns to pay off some of its debt, TT said.
In 1996, the government borrowed 21.0 billion crowns.
